pages.text: FU is denominated $(l)by tier$(): a Tier 5 spool stores Tier 5 FU, a Tier 1 spool stores Tier 1 FU. One unit of Tier N FU is worth several units of Tier N-1 (the $(l)conversion ratio$(), set in config).$(br2)Each unit is worth more the higher its tier — tier is value, not just capacity.

pages.title: FU Cost Calculations
pages.text: Each block's FU cost — and its tier — is $(l)derived from its recipe graph$(): crafting, plus optionally smelting and stonecutting. A diamond block costs what its diamonds are worth; stone costs almost nothing.$(br2)A block's material tier sets the minimum machine and spool tier needed to print it.

pages.title: Winding vs Spending
pages.text: Two different rules:$(br)$(li)$(l)Winding$() (making FU) is $(l)exact-tier$(): netherite only winds into a T6 spool$(li)$(l)Spending$() (printing) is $(l)down-only$(): a spool pays any cost at or below its tier, never above$(br2)So your best spools can print anything below them, but cheap materials can't reach a high-tier spool.

pages.title: Lower Tiers Cost More
pages.text: Lower-tier machines pay a higher FU multiplier per block — a Tier 1 printer costs more per block than a Tier 8 Fabricator.$(br2)Printing always costs a little $(l)more$() than the matter is worth. Stack $(l)4 Efficiency modules$() to reach exact break-even (1:1); you can never print matter for less than it's worth. Per-tier efficiencies are in the config.
